inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payment transactions' 243 (millions of yen); Board Incentive Plan trust only. Equity-award taxes nil. Effectively an SBC-zero filer.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,259,136,067 issued less 96,916,062 treasury (incl. BIP trust) = 1,162.22m at 2026-06-30 (H1 FY2026 Tanshin). Diluted EPS differs from basic by 0.08% so the diluted count is the same to three figures. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed (immaterial) and the JPY140bn buyback resolved 2026-08-07 is value-neutral at prices near IV -- the cash was still on the 30 June balance sheet, so neither the cash nor the shares have been adjusted for it.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Bonds and borrowings 661,817 current + 656,506 non-current = 1,318,323; less cash and cash equivalents 216,190; less other current financial assets 744,375 (time deposits and securities beyond three months -- INPEX's own net-D/E definition only nets securities within three months, but these are the liquid reserve being built for Abadi LNG and the Abadi capex is charged in the flows, so the cash must offset). Net debt +357,758 at 2026-06-30. Lease liabilities EXCLUDED (treatment B, lease cost in the flows). Asset retirement obligations (497,675) NOT in the bridge: their accretion runs through finance costs and is inside the leakage calibration. Non-controlling interests (248,382) NOT deducted: NCI profit share is folded into the leakage rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are JPY-reported but USD-commodity-driven. Built in JPY: 10y JGB ~1.7% + beta 1.1 x ERP 5.5% = cost of equity ~7.8%, in line with management's stated ~8% cost of equity; after-tax JPY debt cost ~1% at ~10% of EV gives a blended ~7.1%. Rounded UP to 8.0% WACC because the equity bridge carries JPY1.49tn of IJV loans at book and the terminal value rests on an LNG project not yet sanctioned. Cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows (mid-cycle Brent) and the weights, not in the rate: one WACC for all three scenarios. Management's own WACC is ~6%, which this model deliberately does not use.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B -- leases as operating cost. lease_cost_pct_path 1.0% of revenue covers principal (FY2025 19,019; FY2024 24,160; H1 FY2026 6,145) plus interest (1,347) read off the cash-flow statement and the Securities Report note. Lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt and da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (reported D&A 17.5% of FY2025 revenue less ~1pp ROU).
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows via the leakage rate. cash_tax_rate_path is NOT a statutory tax rate: it is the combined cash tax + NCI + ARO-accretion leakage on EBIT, calibrated so FY0 NOPAT ties to reported attributable profit on an unlevered, ex-interest-income basis. FY2025: attributable 393,836 - after-tax interest income 108,501 x 0.7 + after-tax interest paid 44,677 x 0.7 = 349,100 against EBIT (operating profit) 1,135,440 -> 69.3% leakage; FY2024 gives 70.0%; FY2026 guidance (510,000 less 65,000 non-cash TA-recycling gain) gives ~67%. INPEX's fiscal terms (Australian PRRT + company tax, Abu Dhabi concession tax, Japanese tax) take roughly two-thirds of operating profit, which is why the stock trades at ~3x EV/EBITDA and why P/E, not EV/EBITDA, is the comparable multiple. NCI profit share is ~3pp of the 69%.
inputs.matching_asset_rule: Interest income (108,501 in FY2025, almost all on sponsor loans to Ichthys LNG Pty Ltd, the 67.82%-owned equity-method downstream IJV) is STRIPPED from the flows, and the source asset -- loans receivable 44,008 current + 1,446,168 non-current = 1,490,176 at 2026-06-30 -- is ADDED to the bridge at book via equity_bridge. Book approximates fair value: the loans yield ~7.5% in USD against a long-term processing tariff from the upstream JV. The IJV's equity-method profit (72,099 FY2025) sits inside IFRS operating profit and therefore inside the EBITDA margin, so the equity-method investment (1,134,793) is NOT added to the bridge -- adding it would double count. Dividend income (~12bn) stays in the flows and the small investment-securities line (109,124) stays out of the bridge, consistently.
inputs.mid_cycle_treatment: FY2025 (Brent $68.2, JPY149.6/USD, normal volumes) is treated as the mid-cycle anchor; FY2026 guidance (Brent $81.4, JPY159.2, Abu Dhabi volumes down ~30% in H1 on the Hormuz disruption, ~JPY95bn of 'Profit Booster' one-offs) is taken as year 1 and then reverted in FY2027 to Brent ~$70 / JPY150 with normal volumes less ~5% structural decline. Company sensitivities: $1/bbl = JPY5.5bn attributable, JPY1/USD = JPY3.0bn. Pre-FY2024 J-GAAP EBITDA margins are ~4pp lower than the IFRS series because equity-method income was non-operating under J-GAAP; the IFRS margins (FY2024 72.0%, FY2025 73.9%) are the comparable ones.
inputs.capex_basis: capex_pct_path is TOTAL capital investment on the statutory cash-flow statement, not the CSV's 294,026 (which is E&E + D&P + other PP&E only): FY2025 E&E 28,721 + D&P 262,685 + PP&E 2,620 + equity-method contributions 28,142 + business acquisitions 43,017 + other 12,403 = 377,588 (18.8% of revenue); FY2024 ~356,000 (15.7%). Net loans made are excluded because the loan book is carried in the bridge. FY2026 guidance on the company's IJV-inclusive basis is 676bn of growth investment + 200bn of cash reserves (the reserve is not capex); statutory H1 FY2026 capex was already 241,434 and acquisitions (Block 2E Malaysia $350m, INPEX South West ~JPY60bn, Beetaloo) land in H2, so FY2026 is set at 29%. FY2028-FY2031 carry the Abadi LNG build (INPEX 65% of a ~US$20bn project, FID targeted mid-2027) at 32-34% of revenue; capex falls back toward 20% once Abadi is on stream.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing: operating company, non-US AND commodity-cyclical, so owner-fcf.md plus the adaptations file -- currency-matched WACC, one lease treatment, NCI charged once, matching-asset rule, SBC-zero, risk charged once). Not a bank/REIT/LIC; no live corporate action. First valuation of this ticker, no prior Drivers file. DATA QUALITY: (1) CashAndEquivalents in core_metrics is the strict cash-flow-statement figure and understates liquidity; the 744bn of time deposits/securities in OtherCurrentFinancialAssets (kpis) is included in `cash` here, otherwise the company would wrongly look net-debt-heavy at ~1.1tn. (2) The CSV CapEx line understates true reinvestment by acquisitions and equity-method contributions (~84bn in FY2025); the drivers use the broader basis. (3) EBITDA is IFRS from FY2024 and includes equity-method income; earlier J-GAAP years are not margin-comparable. (4) Year 1 is FY2026, of which ten months have elapsed at the valuation date; end-of-year discounting is kept for cross-ticker comparability. (5) Price is the regular Tokyo close, not an after-hours print. SBC-zero: house and street bases coincide, band_position should be read as null.

equity_bridge.item: Loans receivable (current 44,008 + non-current 1,446,168) at book -- principally sponsor loans to Ichthys LNG Pty Ltd (equity-method IJV); their interest income is stripped from the flows
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 Tanshin statement of financial position, 2026-06-30. Matching-asset rule: income out of flows, asset into bridge.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle steady-state revenue growth used in the base path (nominal oil-price drift plus Abu Dhabi expansion net of Japan domestic decline), NOT a historical CAGR: every CAGR here is an artefact of where the oil cycle sat at the endpoints (FY2020 Brent $42 trough, FY2022 $100 peak). Equity CAGR is rejected as a retained-earnings artefact of a cyclical that also buys back ~2-3% of its shares a year.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.6% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 21.1% and FCF 5yr CAGR 26.1% differ by more than 30%: the FY2020 base year was the COVID oil trough (Brent $42, attributable loss of JPY111.7bn). FY2020 EPS was negative so the 5yr EPS CAGR is undefined.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less interest income): FY2020 91.3bn, FY2022 458.5bn, FY2025 291.1bn. Owner FCF is 27% below reported in FY2025 because the IJV loan interest is stripped (SBC is nil). Interest income grew from 33bn (FY2020) to 125bn (FY2024) as the Ichthys project finance was refinanced with sponsor loans, so the owner-FCF CAGR runs below the reported one on the 3yr window (-14.0% vs -8.6%).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = August guidance (1,973bn, -1.9%). FY2027 reverts to mid-cycle Brent ~$70 / JPY150 with Abu Dhabi volumes restored but ~5% structural decline vs FY2025 (-1.0%). FY2028-32 +2%/yr: nominal price drift plus Upper Zakum / Bab expansion net of Japan domestic decline. FY2033-35 +5/+7/+6%: Abadi LNG (INPEX 65% of 9.5 Mtpa) ramping from 2033, assumed one year later than management's 'early 2030s'. FY2035 revenue ~2.57tn, roughly +28% on FY2025 against management's +60% CFFO target -- a deliberately partial credit for Vision 2035.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 81% reproduces guided operating profit of 1,223bn (1,973 x 81% - 1% lease - 19% D&A = 1,203bn). Mid-cycle 73.5-74% is FY2025's 73.9% at $68 Brent; eases to 73% as Abadi's early high-cost years dilute.
base.tax_rationale: 67% in the guidance year (Australian investment incentives ~30bn), 69% thereafter per the FY2025 unlevered calibration. This is tax + NCI + ARO accretion on EBIT, not a statutory rate.
base.terminal_rationale: 1% nominal growth (oil demand plateau, LNG longer) and a 12x owner-FCF cap for a cyclical. Terminal-year capex 20% vs D&A 18% keeps the resource base replaced. At 8%/1% Gordon is 14.4x so the cap binds.

bull.rationale: Brent holds ~$80 / JPY155 through the decade (Pacific-basin LNG shortfall, energy-security policy), Abu Dhabi volumes fully restored in 2027 plus expansion, Abadi on management's timetable (first gas 2032) and Ichthys backfill/Train 3 credit from 2032; approaches the 800 kboe/d Vision 2035 target. Same WACC and leakage as base: the upside is in the flows, not the rate.

bear.rationale: Brent $60 / JPY140 from 2027 (LNG oversupply wave, demand slowdown) with the Hormuz disruption lingering into 2027: revenue -16%, IFRS margin 68% (vs 60% J-GAAP at $42 in FY2020). Abadi slips and is scaled back -- capex is still spent at 27-29% through the build but no Abadi revenue arrives inside the horizon, and the terminal is capped at 10x with zero growth for a depleting base and carbon-transition multiple compression. Ichthys impairment risk is in the margin, not a separate charge.

scenario_narratives.base: INPEX is a two-thirds-taxed cash machine bolted to Ichthys LNG and Abu Dhabi crude, so the valuation turns on three things: where mid-cycle Brent sits in yen, how much of the next five years' cash goes into Abadi LNG before it produces anything, and whether the JPY1.49tn of IJV loans is treated as the asset it is. Base: FY2026 at guidance (record profit on $81 oil, a weak yen and ~95bn of one-offs despite Abu Dhabi shipping constraints), reverting in 2027 to the FY2025 mid-cycle template ($70, JPY150, 73.5-74% IFRS EBITDA margin, 69% leakage); capex peaks at 32-34% of revenue in 2028-31 for Abadi, which starts contributing from 2033 and lifts FY2035 revenue ~28% above FY2025. Terminal value binds at 12x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Higher-for-longer: $80 Brent and JPY155 hold, the Pacific-basin LNG shortfall management describes materialises, Abu Dhabi volumes recover fully and expand, and Abadi reaches FID mid-2027 and first gas in 2032 alongside Ichthys backfill. Production approaches the Vision 2035 800 kboe/d target and FY2035 revenue is ~55% above FY2025 on a 75.5-76% margin.
scenario_narratives.bear: Oversupply and transition: $60 Brent / JPY140 from 2027 with the Middle East disruption lingering, Abadi slipping past the horizon while its build capex is still largely spent, no Train 3, Japan domestic declining, and a 10x zero-growth terminal reflecting a depleting base under carbon pressure. Ichthys impairment and labour risk sit inside the lower margin.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: a price-taker with a live geopolitical binary (Hormuz) on its largest crude asset, a single unsanctioned mega-project (Abadi) absorbing most of the next five years' free cash, and Ichthys concentration ~45% of oil and gas assets. Bull cut to 25%: it needs oil, FX, Abadi timing and Ichthys backfill all to go right at once. Base 50%: FY2025 is a clean mid-cycle template and management's guidance record in 2026 has been conservative.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF for a commodity-cyclical E&P: year 1 at guidance, then revert to the FY2025 template rather than extrapolating a Middle-East-conflict year. Flows are unlevered and attributable-only through a calibrated 69% tax/NCI leakage on EBIT (INPEX's fiscal regimes make EBITDA multiples meaningless; earnings multiples are the comparable). The Ichthys IJV loan book is carried in the bridge at book with its interest stripped from the flows; the equity-method stake is left in the flows via operating profit. Heavy Abadi build capex is charged explicitly for 2028-31 with only partial revenue credit inside the horizon, which is the main reason the value does not sit far above a 0.76x P/B price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle oil and yen: every $1/bbl is ~JPY5.5bn and every JPY1/USD ~JPY3.0bn of attributable profit; the base assumes $70 / JPY150 from 2027
Abadi LNG: FID mid-2027 is not taken; ~JPY2tn of INPEX-share capex is charged with revenue credit only from 2033 -- a cancellation would remove both, a cost overrun only the revenue
Loan book at book value (JPY1,282/share): depends on Ichthys upstream production sustaining the processing tariff through the 2030s (backfill needed)
Leakage rate: the 69% calibration moves ~2pp year to year with PRRT, Abu Dhabi cost recovery and NCI distributions; 1pp of leakage is ~JPY11bn/yr of owner FCF
Strait of Hormuz / Abu Dhabi: H1 FY2026 crude volumes were -23%; a prolonged closure is the bear case's first leg
Terminal multiple: 12x owner FCF (2.4x terminal EV/EBITDA, ~10.5x NOPAT) is modestly above today's ~10x core EV/owner-FCF; implied_exit_multiple is reported per scenario
